findings.issue: The shown-brief check is keyed on the --head string as typed. shown_brief_path uses return_start_key(head), and the brief writes its record under the full 40-char head. cmd_file_return only checks the head against _HEAD_SHAPE ^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$ and never expands it; only drive-phase.py submit expands it (whole_head, :4360). So a phase return filed straight through `audit-task.py file-return P125 --role reviewer --head 6652cd60` with no --shown finds no record (FileNotFoundError -> (None, None)) and files unchecked. That is the silent omission R166 asked to make loud. The same short key also gives the return file a different name from the one the full head would get.
findings.resolution: In cmd_file_return, resolve a phase return's --head to the full commit (git rev-parse --verify <head>^{commit}, as whole_head does) before the record lookup and phase_return_rel use it. If git cannot answer, refuse a short head. Add a case to _recorded_brief_cases that files with _HD_HEAD[:12] and no --shown, and must be refused.

findings.issue: A falsifier the executor declared on attempt 1 becomes 'the plan's', and on a `retry` it cannot be replaced. record_falsifiers keeps only `declared` keys `not in planned`. After `retry` (a new start, so falsifiersRecorded is unmarked), the plan already holds attempt 1's entry, and attempt 2's corrected falsifier is dropped with no line in `did`. falsifier_rule also stops asking the attempt-2 executor for one, because the entry is now held. Yet the decide-falsifier rule (:317-319) says 'could-not-run is no kill - fix the falsifier, then retry'. For an executor-produced falsifier with a wrong find, a non-green unmutated copy or a timeout, `retry` spends attempts on the same could-not-run until maxAttempts. The only ways out are a human `scope --falsifiers` overwrite or `accept`. No case covers a retry after a falsifier stop.
findings.resolution: Record where each entry came from, e.g. the start of the return that declared it. Let a later start's return replace an entry an earlier start's return recorded, while a planner-written entry still wins. Or show the held falsifier in the retry brief and ask for a replacement. At minimum, name a dropped declaration in `did`. Add a case: survivor, then retry, then a corrected falsifier is filed, then it is killed.

preExisting.issue: This is why P125.142's red-first reads could-not-prove. The cause is not that the stage is absent at HEAD: new_stage_baseline exists to accept exactly that case. The problem is that new_stages joins the string literals of EVERY declared test file at HEAD into one set. At 4b7df26b, plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py already holds a "fp-block" literal (git show 4b7df26b:plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py | grep -c '"fp-block"' prints 1). So 'fp-block' read as not new, and the unknown-stage failure at HEAD (0/1) was graded as HEAD being red. The helper's own run did show test_drive_phase.py failing on assertions, 3/6 with fp1 among them. The function predates the phase base (d24b3047, P123.51).
preExisting.resolution: Work out new stages per test file, from the file the command runs (the path in its argv), and not from the join of all declared files. Add a case where two declared suites share a stage label and only the commanded one adds it.
